answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating each node demands staking collateral that scales exponentially: like surviving a harsh tundra, solitary nodes thrive, but rogue swarms face exponential capital exhaustion. A forged juniper identity or counterfeit crystal credential costs superlinearly more to mint, rendering mass agent replication economically ruinous.
